title: Research: the recursion lever on #2979 and #3945; the full cut on #2979's words with a re-solved table, b = 1.7887046e-3 for the DFT, checked by computer (Lean proofs up to 1.7806935e-3; no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Headline (checked by computer, not proved in Lean).** On Marius-Paul Dumitrean's #2979 words
(`research/rank7-joint-endframes`, unchanged, read in place from main) with a table of hosts that I re-solved for
the full cut (A-fc, carried in `fills/2979Fc/`), removing each of the 16,576 literal heads (job 25 on its array)
gives **b = 1.7887045643e-3** for the DFT, certified at 17,887,045/10^10 (`verify.py --instance 2979Fc`, registered).
That table's own figure with no lever is 1.6897030e-3, below #2979's 1.7290340e-3: it pays off only with the full
cut, and the community's admission rejects it at its strict-gain steps, by design (details below). It is not proved
in Lean; the same full cut is proved in Lean on #3945 with every head kept, at 1.7806935e-3.

**Result on #2979's published table.** A change of the recursion, not of the word, raises the complex-side figure
from b = 1.7290339826e-3 to **b = 1.7556473153e-3** (+1.539 %). It is a saving for the discrete Fourier transform in OpenAI's exact-arithmetic
machine model. On Dugongue's #3945 the same lever gives 1.7501109246e-3, and on #3945 with every head kept (its words
and price, with a table of hosts re-solved by the community's own allocation programs so that every block that can be
a head stays empty, carried in this package) **1.7581520168e-3**; on that table the *full cut* (each head removed,
job 25 on its array, every other rank-48 block split into two blocks of 24 on the same role) gives
**1.7806935406e-3**. I have proved those DFT bounds in Lean (below), the highest at **1.7806935e-3**. **No κ is
claimed.**

**The change (the lever).** In #2979's unit, 16,086 of the 28,190 rank-48 blocks per round (8,064 in child 8, 8,022 in
child 10) are literal heads: the first non-identity operation on their own array, acting on that array alone, with
nothing hosted there before. I cut each head by 24 of its 48 axes, so that its array takes a job of 49 axes while
every other array keeps the full 73. The recursion then feeds the word with jobs of two sizes in a fixed ratio
(50,218 : 16,086 arrays per round). Theorem 1G (`PROOF.md`) shows that such a recursion runs at the speed of its
balance, sum_r n_r (r/73)^(1-b) = 50,218 + 16,086 (49/73)^(1-b), provided every paid block is smaller than every job
(48 < 49).

**Changed hypothesis.** The community's recursion gives every array the same job; the ceiling tool assumes it. The
mixed-target recursion changes that coverage law, so, as the card's allowed variation says, I give Theorem 1G as the
replacement bound and do not apply the incumbent ceiling. Nothing else changes in the lever: no gate, no axis between children, no
endpoint; on #2979's published table no allocation row changes either, while A-fc and the tables with every head
kept are re-solved tables of hosts (described below and in README sections 7 and 9).

**Status of the headline A-fc.** Checked by computer here (`verify.py --instance 2979Fc`, both parts): the table
pinned by sha256, 16,576 literal heads (8,288 + 8,288) and no other rank-48 block in my network, the global profile
equal to `fills/2979Fc/PROFILE.json`, the uniform root equal to the community's own root for this table to 24 digits,
the full-cut price, and the exact rate certificate at 17,887,045/10^10, refused one step higher. Proved in Lean,
outside this repository: Theorem 1G (`Eng.engine_seam_final`) and the general theorem of the full cut
(`cut_heads_full`, `Work/Mixed/Bridge/CoreF`), as used on #3945 with every head kept. **Not in Lean: A-fc's own
instance** (its heads-first certificate, the cut fact on #2979's words, which is argued from the template it shares
with #3945's, and the rate fact at 17,887,045/10^10).

**How A-fc's table was made, and the community's checks on it.** A class solution of a mixed-integer program on
#3815's Hall model, then #3815's own reverse-time placement (Erwan Secousses' / ChaloupeMusic's `build_fill.py`) in a
tolerant mode: a role with no planned slot left at its call goes to a spare bin that is open at that call, is not a
head bin, is not yet used at that call and has room. Nine roles were placed that way (8 of width 6 at call 553, 1 of
width 4 at call 0), and 8 planned width-6 slots stayed idle. However it was made, the table is checked as a table:
run unmodified on a fresh clone at the base, #2979's checks pass it, including #2979's PR2839 owner engine (271,728
roles, T = 74, its seven corruption controls rejected), `check_allocation.py`'s pins, words, PROVIDERS, physical
count 66,813 and 5 rejection controls, the exact moment auditor (root 1.6897030e-3), `check_cap.py`'s cap
certificate, rank mass and local profile, and the complete replay up to the admission (fresh natives, owners, parent
lift, rebind, discovery 7 of 7, outer ledger with 63 positive checks). It is rejected exactly where the lower figure
1.6897030e-3 is compared with a higher one: the moment auditor's strict gain (`audit_allocation_moment.py` line 65),
the complete admission (`admit_extension.py` line 388), and the release's strict-gain list (at PR2269); and by
`check_cap.py`'s `recorded gap` (line 68), which is a near-optimality bound on #2979's own claim (root within 1e-6 of
the cap; A-fc's gap is 3.93e-5), not literally a strict-gain check. The community's moment engine cannot price A-fc's
model with two job sizes: its halving constraint m^2 > 2 r_max^2 holds for the uniform model (5,329 > 2 * 48^2 = 4,608) and
fails for the job of 25 (625 < 2 * 23^2 = 1,058). The 1.7887046e-3 comes from my own pricing under Theorem 1G, which has no such
condition (the full cut on #3945 with every head kept, 625 < 1,152, is proved in Lean the same way).

**Status of the other instances.** Construction plus proof. Checked by computer here: my conversion of both words, the head count, the
global profile (equal to `PROFILE.json` digit for digit), the uniform root (equal to `complex_lower` to 24 digits), the
half-cut price, and an exact rational certificate of the rate inequality at the figure, refuted one grid step higher.
Proved in Lean, outside this repository: the DFT bound (OpenAI's `UniformFourier` statement with only the exponent and
the names changed), with Theorem 1G and the cut theorems inside that proof.

**Remaining obligations.** (0) A-fc's instance in Lean (open question 3). (1) Whether the outer step for integer multiplication accepts a supplier with two job
sizes is open; that is why no κ is claimed. For orientation only: b is above the selected bit side c = 1.7334270e-3
(#589), so the bit side would bind. (2) The cut is not replayed in the community's exact eight-stream operator model
(checked in my lowering and network, and in Lean for the DFT). (3) The halving guard m^2 > 2R^2 of the outer recipe
holds for the half cut (49^2 > 2 * 24^2; argued, not checked) but fails for the full cut, the headline included
(25^2 = 625 < 2 * 23^2 = 1,058; < 1,152 on #3945), so the outer recipe as written does not take the full cut; one
more reason no κ is claimed.

## Task and overlap

- Base `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244`. Inputs: ten files of #2979 on main (head
  `be191346391661f4d35fc0d1508d0a6029572576`), pinned by Git blob and sha256 in `SOURCES.json` and declared in
  `VERIFY.json`. No foreign commit; nothing of #2979 is copied.
- Card `complex-new-helper-inventory` (the card #2979 and #3945 used), `scope_status: changed`, reason in `TASK.json`.
  It also bears on `independent-moment` (my head test and lowering are an independent reconstruction of #2979's paid
  profile from its words and FILL rows) and `formal-interface-lemma` (the Lean statements in README section 5).
- Second instance: Dugongue's #3945 (head `91f81d131252db704f945891da1ea54e29d46b8b`, archived on main on 20 October 2026 with the same files):
  57,312 heads, b = 1.7501109246e-3, with the same programs (`verify.py --instance 3945`, README section 6). Not
  registered: its files were on an open pull request when this package was made.
- Third instance: #3945 with every head kept (`verify.py --instance 3945H`, README section 7): the same words, order,
  dispatch, plan, template and global profile, the table of hosts `fills/3945H/FILL.json.gz` (made with the
  allocation programs #3945 uses, with one added condition; #3945's complete stated verification passes on it, 119 of
  119 controls rejected): 80,640 heads (40,320 + 40,320), b = 1.7581520168e-3, certified at 17,581,520/10^10. Not
  registered either, for the same reason.
- Headline instance A-fc (`verify.py --instance 2979Fc`, registered, README section 9): #2979's words with the table
  `fills/2979Fc/FILL.json.gz` (sha256 7fc766c6c3e1561cee60b258138a918020b96d85ea782a2b01ad0ee035fd082e) and its
  paid profile; 16,576 heads removed, no split needed, every paid block of rank at most 23 < 25; b = 1.7887045643e-3,
  certified at 17,887,045/10^10, refused one step higher, with a single head, with one head fewer and with the heads
  kept as blocks of 48. The programs that made the table, its class solution and the commands to re-create it are in
  the Lean repository (`research/record-track/programs/a-fc/`, `research/record-track/data/a-fc/`).
- Fourth instance: the full cut on #3945 with every head kept (the table of `3945H`; `verify.py --instance 3945F`,
  README section 8): the 80,640 heads
  removed (job 25 on their arrays) and the 57,312 other rank-48 blocks split 24 + 24, so every paid block has rank
  at most 24 < 25; b = 1.7806935406e-3, certified at 17,806,935/10^10 and refused one step higher, with the figure
  also refused for a single head, one head fewer and the profile without the split. Not registered either.
- Nearest work and what this adds: the idle-axis chain retracted on 18 and 19 October (#3184, #3190, #3198, #3200,
  #3251; #3934 to #3959, after #4046) moved idle axes between children and changed the exact operator; this package
  moves nothing and keeps the operator, it changes the job taken by the head arrays. The audits of #2979 (#2993,
  #3053, #3079, #3093, #3236, #3237, #3238, #3245, #3285, #3411, #3436, #3441; open #3911 and #3923, and #3585, archived on 20 October) found no
  defect; none uses jobs of two sizes. "Lever" in `research/complex-local-word-ceiling` (`levers.py`) names budget
  screens of the local word, an unrelated use of the word. I found no pull request with a recursion of two job sizes.
  Newest complex figures when I wrote this (20 October 2026, 03:00 EDT, after that morning's archive merges; read again at 13:03 EDT, up to #4211): #4181
  (open) 1.7309803e-3, a fill that attains the pooled ceiling certified in #4091 (a ceiling, not a construction);
  #4100 and #4088 1.7309791e-3, #4085 1.7309704e-3, #4076 1.7308090e-3, archived on main. The
  headline is above every complex-side construction claimed on the hub by others; some research notes there print
  higher ceilings, targets or hypothetical ledgers (for example the archived #3974, and the widened-window ledger of
  #2705 / #2595), which are not constructions.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/lever-mixed-targets-2979 --install-deps
# = python3 -B research/lever-mixed-targets-2979/verify.py --part main      (PASS_LEVER_MIXED_TARGETS_2979_MAIN)
#   python3 -B research/lever-mixed-targets-2979/verify.py --part controls  (PASS_LEVER_MIXED_TARGETS_2979_CONTROLS)
#   python3 -B research/lever-mixed-targets-2979/verify.py --instance 2979Fc --part main      (PASS_LEVER_MIXED_TARGETS_2979Fc_MAIN)
#   python3 -B research/lever-mixed-targets-2979/verify.py --instance 2979Fc --part controls  (PASS_LEVER_MIXED_TARGETS_2979Fc_CONTROLS)
```

Standard library only. On a clean clone at the base, with Python 3.12.3 on Linux: `--check-only` passes, the
registered replay passes in about 5 minutes (peak 0.28 GB) and leaves `git diff --exit-code` clean, the planner selects
only this package, the onboarding tests pass, `check_research_commit.py --check-source-history` passes, and the diff
against the base touches only this folder. The hosted checks will wait for maintainer approval.

Evidence inside the check: both words transported to the native canonical form and replayed exactly on all 632
columns in both orientations, lowered with residual widths equal to #2979's helper by helper, and seven wrong versions
of each rejected; the head test on all 271,728 FILL rows (every role in a window, no bin over its rank, global
profile = `PROFILE.json`); the price; the rate certificate on the half-cut profile derived from the measured heads,
equal to the histogram of the Lean rate module. For the headline A-fc the same checks run on its own table and paid
profile (`fills/2979Fc/`): the head test, the price under the full cut (jobs of 73 and 25) and the rate certificate
on its full-cut profile, which has no Lean rate module.

Failure controls: moving gate A4 before its climb leaves no heads; deleting gate C2 turns the 12,104 other rank-48
blocks into tails; the T74 regression finds the 11,010 heads of the first head test; the figure is refused with a
single head, with one head fewer (16,085), for a profile that is not separated, and one grid step above.

Lean (not run by this repository's checks): [jacobalansussman/wht-power-saving-lean](https://github.com/jacobalansussman/wht-power-saving-lean)
at `563b4e6e913625637f36ba7869bf5fcd0dd4975a`, for the full cut on #3945 with every head kept theorems `OAI.PowerSaving.transform_mainL3945F` and
`OAI.PowerSaving.convolution_mainL3945F`, exponent 1 - 17806935/10^10, axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`,
`Quot.sound` only, one step stronger refused; the same for #3945 with every head kept (half cut) at 1.7581520e-3,
#2979 at 1.7556473e-3, #2979 with every head kept at 1.7564707e-3 and #3945 at 1.7501109e-3 (one package each,
README section 5). The official comparator, with the Lean kernel and nanoda, accepts it against OpenAI's statement at this exponent and rejects the statement one step stronger. Prepared for the Lean
leaderboard bigospeedrun.com/exact-dft as a pull request to bigospeedrun/verifier adding submissions/dft/jacobalansussman-lever-3945-full-cut (meant to be opened alongside this one; I will add its link and its robot's receipt as a comment once it is open). The package's
programs (`tools/*.py`) and `network/` files equal, byte for byte, files of that commit (pairs of paths in `SOURCES.json`).

Checks not run: A-fc's instance in Lean; the cut in the community's eight-stream operator model; the outer step; the halving-guard question;
any κ assembly.

table A-fc (its class solution and the tolerant placement), my conversion and head test, the
rate certificate and the Lean proofs. The new files were written by AI agents (Claude) under my direction; no person outside this project has
reviewed them. Apache-2.0; `NOTICE` lists every copied file and its source.

## Open next questions

README section *Open next questions* and `TASK.json` `open_questions`. The smallest useful follow-up is the replay of
the cut of a sample of heads in the community's exact eight-stream operator model (#3187's replay, as #4046 used),
with a control that a wrong cut changes the operator. Blocker: none. The largest is the outer step with two job
sizes; it needs a precise statement of the outer theorem's supplier hypotheses.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

`--print-card` and the pin rules made the metadata easy to get right. What I missed is a documented way to bind a
proof that lives in another public Git repository (here a Lean proof): the package records the commit and a
byte-equality of the shared files, but no pin form covers it.
